scope: One metadata/image-SHA/PIL-header geometry pairing execution only. No processor, RGB decode, model, QA forward, prediction, scoring, training, Tiny CPU gate, or second-stage admission.
findings: The consumer does not inspect answer/reference or prediction fields for selection. It parses source-container rows to access only fixed DEV IDs, images and task/source metadata.

SPLIT and manifest are checked against the existing screen READY; each source file and each selected image are hashed against the sealed metadata. PIL is used for image dimensions without RGB conversion or pixel loading.
Geometry buckets include task, image count and ordered post-area-cap integer dimensions. The 401408-area-cap calculation matches the current declared input policy.

The fixed hash-ordered augmenting-path matching constructs a complete target/donor bijection or excludes the entire bucket. Different known groups and disjoint image SHA sets prohibit self/same-group or exact-image reuse.

The coverage gate is implemented as stated: at least 8 medical QA in at least 2 medical tasks and at least 2 other domains each with at least 8 QA. This is an investment gate, not a power, quality, or semantic-validity claim.
Successful first-stage coverage would establish geometric constructability only. Actual text/placeholder/mask/position/packed-layout equality remains unverified and separately gated.
limitations: The source TRAIN containers include DEV and are parsed to select those IDs; no claim is made that the container bytes exclude FIT answers. Answer values are not used to form the pairing.
Image hashes require reading complete image-file bytes even though image content is not decoded; these reads and the PIL header work are charged.
Different groups and image SHA disjointness do not establish statistical independence, absence of near-duplicates, semantic modality matching, or that a donor makes the original gold false.
The selected subset is geometry-conditioned, drawn from explored DEV, and evaluated under one fixed permutation; coverage is not representative by guarantee.
Both time caps and the once-only rule require the external supervisor; the consumer itself has no hard timeout and only rejects an already existing PAIRING output.

The second-stage section is a conditional scientific plan only. Neither a pass nor the presence of this protocol authorizes checkpoint/model loading or NLL requests. Its actual full-answer target and numerical path still require source review.
No automatic mask/seed/size relaxation, subset rescue, data expansion, closed-branch repair or new model activation follows.
closure_rule: If the fixed coverage gate fails, close this diagnostic without changing matching rules or expanding data. If it passes, only a separately reviewed bounded model proposal may be considered.
review_execution: Static source/protocol review only; the consumer was not imported or run, and no QA, image, model or tensor was opened during this review.
